predicted.label: Forecast demand
predicted.scale_note: QUEBEC_CITY_POPULATION_SHARE = 839311/8501833; converts province-scale model output to the Quebec City CMA the sim is calibrated to. Tune if model bias differs.

actual.label: Realized demand
actual.horizon_basis_note: T7/T30 jobs predict daily demand × horizon (a cumulative total); realized_demand is a per-day rate. horizon_basis lifts realized onto the model's horizon basis (× dashboard_horizon days) so both series share units. T1 (horizon 1) is unchanged.

actual.label: Realized stockout rate (7d)
actual.source_note: The model predicts P(stockout within 7 days); the honest comparator is the realized frequency of that event (fraction of entities that hit stockout in a trailing 7-day window), NOT the instantaneous shortage rate. Residual gap is genuine model calibration error — do NOT swap back to shortage_rate to force overlay.

actual.label: Realized stockout rate (7d)
actual.source_note: p_stockout_by_7d is a 7-day cumulative stockout probability; compared against the realized 7-day stockout frequency (same event, same horizon). Residual gap is genuine hazard-model calibration error.

predicted.label: Forecast wastage
predicted.scale_note: QUEBEC_CITY_POPULATION_SHARE = 839311/8501833; the expiry-waste model is trained at province scale, so its summed output is divided down to the Quebec City CMA the sim realizes. Residual gap after scaling is genuine model/sim bias (e.g. few in-window expiries on a 42-day shelf life) — do NOT tune scale to force overlay.

predicted.label: Forecast supply
predicted.scale_note: QUEBEC_CITY_POPULATION_SHARE = 839311/8501833; the supply-forecast model is trained at province scale, so its summed output is divided down to the Quebec City CMA the sim realizes. Residual gap after scaling is genuine model/sim bias — do NOT tune scale to force overlay.

chart.stockout_note: stockout_window_hours (default 168 = 7 days) matches the risk/hazard models' P(stockout within 7d) horizon; an entity counts as stocked-out when current_stock_units <= stockout_threshold (0 = literally empty). Raise the threshold toward the safety floor if the sim's per-type pools rarely hit exact zero.
chart.window_note: forecast_interval_hours commits ONE validation point per simulated day (the demand model's 1-day horizon) and measures realized demand over the whole day -> honest, no 6h annualization spikes; the predictions table still updates every tick. Set 0 for legacy per-tick cadence, where realized_smoothing_hours smooths the actual line instead. usage_window_*_hours size the model's trend-feature windows (tick ~6h).
